subject: Indemnity split proposal — defend vs. reimburse (Orchid AI order form)
messages:

Cc: David Lee <david.lee@orchid.ai>; legal@orchid.ai
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Orchid Order Form redline — indemnity allocation questions

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to move forward. We attached a redline of the Order Form (Orchid_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf) with a few open items on indemnity. High level questions:

- For third-party IP claims tied to model output, Orchid is asking for Redwood to defend and indemnify. We understand this is sensitive for you given open model vectors and training sources.
- We proposed removing the carve-out for "customer-provided content" only where customer materially controls the prompt templates or provided training data. Can you confirm if Redwood can accept a defend obligation in that narrower case?
- We flagged insurance/offset language — would Redwood accept an insurance-first waterfall (insurer pays first, then vendor)?

Attached is our redline and a short example scenario that motivated the ask. Can you loop in your legal folks and let us know feasible compromises by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Claire Jackson
Head of Partnerships | Orchid AI
Claire Jackson, Orchid AI

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Claire Jackson <claire.jackson@orchid.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai; rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Order Form redline — indemnity allocation questions

Claire — appreciate the clear redline and scenario. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Rishi (contracts) to weigh in. Quick summary from our side before legal chimes in:

- We understand Orchid's concern and are prepared to propose a compromise rather than broad defend-for-any-output.
- Preliminary commercial posture: Redwood could accept defend for third-party IP claims that (a) relate to outputs generated solely from proprietary customer data supplied by Orchid for fine-tuning or prompt templates that Orchid explicitly provided and controlled, and (b) exclude claims arising from downstream customer modifications or customer redistribution.
- We need to maintain an OSS/training-data carve-out: claims based on pretraining or third-party datasets we use or model variants we host will remain excluded.

Next steps I propose: Kimberly and Rishi to provide specific redline language (narrow defend scope + cap/insurance mechanics). Then we propose a 30-min call with Orchid legal to walk through the compromise and timing for signature. Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai; Claire Jackson <claire.jackson@orchid.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-09T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Order Form redline — indemnity allocation questions

Ben / Claire — I reviewed the attached redline and Ben's suggested compromise. Below are trackable edits and our recommended commercial/legal guardrails. I'm attaching a proposed counter-redline (RDW_indemnity_counterproposal.docx). Key points:

1) Narrow defend trigger
- Proposed language: "Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer from third-party claims alleging IP infringement to the extent (and only to the extent) that such claim arises directly from (i) Customer Content that was provided to Redwood for the purpose of training or fine-tuning a specific model used under this Order Form, or (ii) prompts or prompt templates that were authored and materially controlled by Customer and used verbatim in generation of the allegedly infringing output."

2) Explicit exclusions
- Exclude: (a) outputs reflecting pre-training data sources or general model behavior; (b) outputs after Customer materially modified the generated content or redistributed it with additional content; (c) claims attributable to Customer's failure to follow usage policies.

3) Insurance/offset waterfall
- We can accept an insurance-first approach but ask that Redwood's indemnity obligation be primary to the extent the insurer denies coverage for bad faith or other reasons. Proposed mechanics in the docx.

4) Cap / allocation
- Recommend a monetary cap tied to the Order Form value (e.g., 2x annual subscription for defend/reimburse remediation), with carveouts for willful misconduct. Also propose an expedited notice-and-cooperation clause and a short SLA for Redwood to take control of defense ("right to assume defense") with counsel approval thresholds.

5) Operational ask
- If Orchid accepts the narrow trigger, ops needs a simple evidence pathway: timestamped archive of Customer Content used for fine-tuning / clear prompt template labeling. Ben / Rishi — will your teams be able to commit to recordkeeping for deals that accept this clause?

I can join a customer call if helpful. If Orchid is ok with the language, we'll drop the counter-redline into your DocuSign-ready Order Form.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments: RDW_indemnity_counterproposal.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Claire Jackson <claire.jackson@orchid.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai; rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-10T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Order Form redline — indemnity allocation questions

Claire — following Kimberly's note (below) we've prepared a narrow, operationally-feasible compromise: defend where Orchid supplied the training dataset or provided a labeled prompt template that was used verbatim; exclude the model pretraining and general behavior. We attached Redwood's proposed redline (RDW_indemnity_counterproposal.docx) and a short evidence checklist Orchid would need to accept (timestamps, dataset manifest, prompt-template registry).

Proposal summary (short):
- Defendant obligation: Redwood to defend/reimburse for qualifying third-party IP claims tied to customer-supplied training data or verbatim prompts.
- Exclusions: pretraining/OSS, post-generation modifications, policy violations.
- Insurance: accept insurer-first but Redwood's indemnity remains where insurer denies coverage.
- Cap: 2x ARR for the Order Form term; standard carveouts for willful misconduct.

Would you be open to a 30-minute legal call Tuesday 8/12 at 10:00am PT to walk through the specific redline? If so, I'll send calendar invite and upload the DocuSign-ready order form to the HubSpot deal (link below).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.
Ben
